difficulty.notes: Vue/webpack user-center bundle. The anchor is the submit handler callback (login.js, the 1.json answer): it builds the payload password = this.encode(this.encrypt(password)) and posts via this.login(o). encrypt/encode are Vue-prototype methods from the crypto module ed08 in app.js (prototype.encrypt=I.e=u, prototype.encode=I.d=encodeURIComponent wrapper, prototype.decrypt=I.b=p). Graded chain (cross-file into app.js): u (AES-ECB fixed-key G3JH98Y8MY9GWKWG + url-encode, 0.7), the encode/encodeURIComponent utility (0.5); decrypt p is off-chain (0). A clean 0.2 sink is not isolable: this.login is a Vuex mapped action and the AES math is cross-file CryptoJS (r.a.AES). Volcengine/iwt/caixinlog analytics are vendor noise.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The login submit handler callback (the 1.json answer): builds the payload password = this.encode(this.encrypt(password)) and posts it. The AES encrypt u (0.7), the encodeURIComponent encode utility (0.5) and the inverse decrypt p (0) are graded below it.

behavior_category.subtype: AES-ECB fixed-key + URL-encoded base64 password token
behavior_category.recompute_check: AES-ECB with the fixed key G3JH98Y8MY9GWKWG is deterministic; 13819912565 -> Wy0AkgthChYWCDF9MwOCyQ== reproduces the sample.

near_categories.why_not: Only the single password field is encrypted; the rest of the payload is plaintext/structural.
It encrypts a credential for a request, not encoded UI/app state.

evidence: this.encrypt/this.encode are Vue-prototype methods injected from another chunk (module ed08); the actual function u is far from its call site.
The same module exports encrypt/decrypt/encode/decode; the login and email-register handlers both call encode(encrypt(password)).
Anchor (encrypt u in app.js) and the submit handler (callback in login.js) live in different chunks, bridged only by a prototype assignment.
